newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Fresenius Medical Care plans issue.
newsitem.headline: German Fresenius Medical Care plans issue.

text.p: German Fresenius Medical Care AG, the world's largest dialysis company, will issue five million new non-voting preference shares worth a nominal 25 million marks ($16.55 million), its parent Fresenius AG said on Friday.

Fresenius Medical Care began operations in September and was created when Fresenius AG merged its global dialysis business with National Medical Care Inc., a unit acquired from U.S. group W.R. Grace Inc.
Dresdner Bank and CS First Boston will lead-manage the share issue. The issue price, to be determined in a book-building procedure, will be closely linked to ordinary share prices.
Fresenius Medical Care shares were trading down four marks at 135 marks on Friday.

The book-building period will run from November 11 through November 22, and the new shares will begin trading on the Frankfurt and New York bourses on November 26, Hansgeorg Hofmann, board member at Dresdner told a news conference.
Initially, the group planned to issue only four million new shares. Dresdner Bank also said there will be a green-shoe oversubscription clause for up to nominally 3.75 million marks.

Analysts said the new issue was the latest step in a welcome trend in which German companies were increasing shareholder value by offering investors a chance to buy more focused companies rather than huge conglomerates.

At the same time, Frensenius Medical Care unveiled its first-ever results, showing the data on a nine-months basis. Net profit, before provisions, jumped eight percent to $43 million but showed a 75-percent fall after provisions.
Sales climbed eight percent to $2.26 billion.

Although shares fell 2.40 marks to 136.60 during the Frankfurt bourse session, analysts said the fall was likely caused by profit-taking after some investors may have had unusually high performance expectations.
The parent company Fresenius AG, which holds just over 50 percent of Fresenius Medical Care, also reported nine-month results, which helped boost the share prices by five marks to 317 marks.
Fresenius AG said acquisitions had a large impact on results and group net profit surged 41 percent to 86 million marks with pre-tax profit rising 38 percent to 153 million marks.
Sales rose 24 percent to 2.04 billion marks.
"Besides stronger sales, a key factor for profits was a lower than proportional rise in other costs," Fresenius said.
Extraordinary earnings from the sale of Schiwa GmbH were more than offset by the costs related to the merger of Fresenius Dialysetechnik and National Medical Care.

Fresenius' drugs business, posting a 14-percent jump in sales to 611 million marks, and the dialysis equipment business, moving ahead 13 percent to 1.04 billion marks, showed the strongest gains. The group posts most of its sales abroad.
Looking ahead to the full year, Fresenius chief executive Gerd Krick said the group is optimistic the trend seen in the first nine months of the year will continue.
"We look for the developments in the next months to keep pace the developments in the last months and expect profits will grow more strongly than sales."
